🔥 Rewind | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Capturing and editing gameplay moments locally without performance impact or cloud dependency.
✨ Key Features: • Instant Replay • Screen and Game Recording • Quick Screenshots • Local Clip Management • Compress and Share
📖 Summary: Rewind was a lightweight, open-source, local-first gaming recorder designed for instant replay, screen recording, and clip editing. It prioritized performance and privacy by avoiding cloud dependencies, accounts, and telemetry, allowing users to capture and manage their gameplay moments locally. Although development has ceased, the project remains available as a public fork.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 contrack | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide individuals with a centralized, self-hosted, and privacy-respecting platform for managing, enriching, and actively tracking their personal and professional contact network.
✨ Key Features: • Import contacts from multiple sources (Apple, Google, LinkedIn, Facebook)
📖 Summary: Contrack is a self-hosted, privacy-focused contact management application designed to consolidate, enrich, and track personal and professional contacts. It aims to give users full ownership of their network by importing contacts from various sources, automatically deduplicating them, enriching profiles with notes and web research, and providing tools to maintain relationships.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ homelable | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Visualizing and monitoring self-hosted homelab infrastructure.
✨ Key Features: • Self-hosted infrastructure visualization • Network, Zigbee, Z-Wave scanning • Live status monitoring • Interactive network diagrams • Device documentation integration
📖 Summary: Homelable is a self-hosted infrastructure visualization tool that scans and monitors your homelab network. It generates interactive network diagrams, provides live status updates, and integrates device documentation directly into the visualization.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 proxmox-manager | Shell
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide a convenient and efficient command-line interface for managing Proxmox VE virtual machines and containers, especially for users who prefer TUI environments or need a lightweight, dependency-free solution.
✨ Key Features: • Single-file Bash TUI • No external dependencies • VM/CT listing and status • Start/stop/restart functionality • Snapshot management
📖 Summary: Proxmox Manager is a single-file Bash script that provides a Text-based User Interface (TUI) for managing Proxmox Virtual Machines (VMs) and Containers (CTs). It offers essential management functions without external dependencies, focusing on ease of use and direct interaction with Proxmox VE.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 wavemon | C
🎯 Primary Use Case: Monitoring the status and performance of wireless network interfaces on Linux systems through a text-based user interface.
✨ Key Features: • Real-time monitoring of wireless network devices • Displays signal and noise levels • Shows packet statistics • Provides device configuration and network parameters • ncurses-based interface for terminal display
📖 Summary: wavemon is a C-based, ncurses-enabled monitoring application for Linux that provides real-time insights into wireless network devices. It displays signal and noise levels, packet statistics, device configuration, and network parameters, working with most Linux kernel-supported wireless hardware.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 ghgrab | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: To efficiently browse and download specific files or folders from remote Git repositories without performing a full clone, directly from the command line.
✨ Key Features: • Browse and download files/folders from GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, Gitea, Forgejo • Terminal User Interface (TUI) for easy navigation and selection • File preview within the TUI
📖 Summary: ghgrab is a command-line interface tool built with Rust that allows users to browse and download specific files or folders from various Git forges like GitHub, GitLab, and others directly from their terminal. It features a user-friendly TUI for easy navigation, file preview, and efficient selection, avoiding the need for full repository clones.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source
